mood.p: Woensdag begint volgens Weeronline op veel plaatsen droog met hier en daar zon, maar in de loop van de middag trekken buien over het land, mogelijk met onweer, bij een maximum van rond de 18 graden en een stevige westenwind aan de kust. Het KNMI rekent op perioden met regen en tijdelijk veel wind. Het is bovendien de dag van de landelijke 24-uursstaking in het openbaar vervoer: geen treinen, bussen, trams of metro's, alleen de sprinter tussen Amsterdam Centraal, Schiphol en Hoofddorp rijdt. De FNV protesteert tegen de bezuinigingen op WW en WIA, een dag nadat duizenden ambtenaren met een nagemaakte gouden koets naar het ministerie van Financien trokken. Met Prinsjesdag op 15 september in zicht en de wegen al vol door de gesloten A28-brug bij Nijkerk wordt het een dag van thuiswerken, fietsen en geduld.

global.h3: US hits targets near Kharg Island as Iran threatens Gulf ports
global.summary: The US military struck Iranian oil tankers and other targets near Kharg Island and the port of Jask on Tuesday 8 September, Fox News reported, and the IRGC responded by telling ship crews in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to evacuate.
body: Bloomberg, citing a Fox News report, said American forces hit targets around Kharg Island, Iran's main crude export terminal, and the southern port city of Jask on Tuesday. Unnamed US officials described the strikes as part of a strategy to squeeze Iran economically and push Tehran toward ending the war that began in February. West Texas Intermediate rose as much as 1.4 percent to above 94 dollars a barrel in early Asian trading on Wednesday after closing 1.7 percent higher on Tuesday.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps warned that vessels anchored or docked in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports hosting US forces would be treated as legitimate targets and told crews to leave immediately, according to the state news agency IRNA. The threat followed a weekend in which US Central Command said it struck three Iranian tankers after the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy ships.

global.h3: Houthi strikes on Saudi cities and oil sites wound 73
global.summary: Yemen's Houthis attacked Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Tuesday 8 September, injuring 73 people and igniting fires at energy facilities, the Saudi-led coalition said.
body: Reuters reported that the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen counted 73 injured civilians, including women and children, after a wave of Houthi drone and missile attacks on southern Saudi Arabia. Fires broke out at several oil facilities and utilities, and operations were temporarily suspended. The southern region hosts the 400,000 barrel a day Jazan refinery, one of the kingdom's largest.

The Houthis said the attacks were retaliation for more than 120 Saudi strikes on Yemen over the previous three days, after weeks of renewed fighting shattered a four-year truce in the civil war. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the escalation dangerous and irresponsible, and Riyadh vowed to respond.

global.h3: Iran to declare Hormuz exclusion zone as tanker traffic dwindles
global.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council said on Monday 7 September it will announce a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz within days, while shipping data showed transits at their lowest since May.
body: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Tehran would soon publish a prohibited zone stretching from the US Navy blockade line through the strait and into the Gulf, where vessels transiting without Iranian permission would be stopped, Reuters reported. Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf separately threatened to target Gulf energy infrastructure, including US oil and gas interests, if American attacks continue.

Al Jazeera reported that Iran also says a deal with Oman to manage shipping through the strait is in its final stages and would include a temporary safe route. Kpler data cited by Reuters showed an average of only about 10 ships a day passing through the waterway on Sunday.

global.h3: Russia resumes Kyiv strikes after three-day pause, two dead
global.summary: Russian drones and missiles hit Kyiv and the Odesa region overnight into Tuesday 8 September, killing at least two people and ending a pause that coincided with US envoy visits.
body: AP reported that at least two people were killed and around ten injured as Russia struck civilian infrastructure at some 16 locations around the Ukrainian capital. President Zelenskyy said residential buildings suffered significant damage. Ukraine answered with drone attacks on Russian territory and on occupied Crimea that officials said killed at least two people.

The strikes followed three days without attacks on Moscow or Kyiv while Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. CBS News said the resumption underlined the limited immediate results of the diplomatic push.

global.h3: Ukraine's prosecutor general quits amid corruption probe
global.summary: Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko submitted his resignation on Monday 7 September, days after anti-corruption agents raided his office.
body: Reuters reported that Kravchenko cited political reasons, saying he did not want the office to be used as an instrument of political confrontation. The Kyiv Independent said his office is accused of running a scheme that took bribes to protect fraudulent call centres while laundering millions of dollars.

The resignation lands at a sensitive moment for Kyiv, which is pressing Western partners for winter support and trying to demonstrate progress on governance. Democracy Now noted the raid by anti-corruption agents came only days before he stepped down.

global.h3: Israeli strikes kill 12 in southern Lebanese town
global.summary: Strikes on Kfar Roummane on Monday 7 September killed at least 12 people including two children and a medic, Lebanon's health ministry said, with no prior evacuation warning.
body: Reuters and the New York Times reported that the Israeli military said it was responding to Hezbollah drone attacks and targeted what it called Hezbollah infrastructure. The attacks came a day after Israeli strikes killed seven people and days after the IDF said it had captured a ridge overlooking Nabatieh.

Despite a ceasefire, Israel says its troops will stay in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed. Residents interviewed by Democracy Now described shrapnel injuries and concussions among children treated at local clinics.

global.h3: Gaza strikes continue as 16 ceasefire violations logged in a day
global.summary: Israeli strikes and shelling killed several Palestinians across Gaza on Tuesday 8 September, including a man hit in a tent north of Nuseirat, as funerals were held for around 100 bodies recovered in Zeitoun.
body: Reuters reported that a weekend strike on a vehicle in western Gaza City killed a man and his eight-year-old daughter, with the IDF saying it had targeted a Hamas militant. A tank shell fired at a school sheltering displaced families killed a three-year-old boy, medics said. Palestinian outlets counted 16 new violations of the October 2025 ceasefire on Tuesday alone.

Families in Gaza City's Zeitoun district buried about 100 people whose remains were pulled from the rubble of buildings destroyed earlier in the war, including 55 members of one family killed in November 2023.

global.h3: West Bank teen shot dead as Netanyahu orders outposts removed
global.summary: A 19-year-old Palestinian was killed and three wounded when settlers and soldiers converged on the village of Hajja on Monday 7 September, a day after Netanyahu reportedly ordered unauthorised outposts dismantled.
body: Reuters reported that villagers confronted nine armed settlers from a nearby outpost and were then trapped by Israeli troops approaching from the other side. In a separate incident a Palestinian who stabbed a settler inside an outpost was shot dead. The UN counts at least 79 Palestinians killed in the West Bank this year, including 19 children.

Sources told Reuters that Prime Minister Netanyahu has ordered unauthorised settler outposts to be dismantled, and Israel's Supreme Court ruled that defence authorities must allow three families chased out of Jalud to return home.

global.h3: Pentagon polygraphed 50 Joint Staff members over leaks
global.summary: About 50 officers and civilians on the US military's Joint Staff were given lie detector tests in August over reports on dwindling missile stocks, the New York Times reported on Tuesday 8 September.
body: The New York Times said investigators asked whether staff had discussed munitions stockpiles, including long-range missiles and Patriot interceptors, with journalists or passed on classified material. The tests followed press reports that the Iran war had depleted key US weapons.

Democracy Now noted that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not briefed the Pentagon press corps on the Iran war since 5 May and has restricted reporters' access inside the building. Reuters separately reported that the White House has reviewed candidates to replace Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg.

global.h3: Canada's counter-tariffs kick in as Trump targets Bombardier
global.summary: Canadian retaliatory tariffs on about 27.6 billion Canadian dollars of US goods took effect at 12:01 am on Tuesday 8 September, hours after Trump said Bombardier jets should no longer be sold in the United States.
body: CNBC reported duties ranging from 15 to 50 percent on hundreds of product lines, with US steel, aluminium and iron facing the top 50 percent rate alongside furniture, motorcycles and clothing. Ottawa described the move as a dollar for dollar response to US Section 338 tariffs on Canadian exports.

On Truth Social the day before, Trump demanded Americans stop buying Bombardier aircraft unless the company builds them in the United States, Reuters and the Washington Post reported. Trade talks between the two countries have stalled.

global.h3: Kremlin open to new talks as US floats winter de-escalation
global.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday 7 September that Moscow does not rule out resuming three-way talks, after Witkoff and Kushner's first joint visit to Kyiv produced no breakthrough.
body: Reuters reported Peskov saying it was too early to say when or where talks might happen. Witkoff spoke of substantive progress after three hours with Putin on Saturday, but Zelenskyy said the visit yielded no deal and that the war will continue, the Kyiv Independent reported.

Zelenskyy told Axios that Washington is testing whether Russia and Ukraine could agree limited steps before and during winter, covering energy and electricity facilities, grain shipments and oil and gas exports, while restarting talks on a broader settlement. He said the message from the envoys was that the Russians are ready to negotiate.

global.h3: AfD's 44% in Saxony-Anhalt rattles Berlin, Merz stays put
global.summary: The far-right AfD won 43.8 percent in Sunday's Saxony-Anhalt state election, the strongest far-right result in Germany since the Nazi era, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday 7 September he will not step down.
body: Reuters reported turnout of 77 percent and a heavy defeat for Merz's CDU. AfD deputy parliamentary leader Beatrix von Storch told the BBC the party is very close to taking power and urged rivals to open coalition talks, though mainstream parties have pledged not to govern with the AfD.
Migrant organisations in the state warned the result will deepen everyday discrimination. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten called the outcome a wake-up call for Europe.

global.h3: Iceland summons US envoy over Trump's flag-covered map
global.summary: Iceland's foreign minister summoned Ambassador Billy Long on Monday 7 September after Trump posted an image showing Iceland and other countries draped in the American flag under the label United States of America.
body: Reuters reported that Foreign Minister Thorgerdur Gunnarsdottir called the post completely inappropriate. The image is the latest in a series of territorial provocations from Trump, who on the same day shared memes renaming New Mexico as New America, prompting Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham to say the state's name is not up for debate.

Russia's foreign ministry meanwhile criticised the deployment of an advanced US missile system to Norway, saying launchers able to reach Moscow dealt another blow to prospects for strategic stability talks.

global.h3: Gulf states hedge on US security as UAE builds new trade routes
global.summary: UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash told the Hili Forum in Abu Dhabi on Monday 7 September that the country is building alternative energy and trade routes so it is not held hostage by the Iran war.
body: Reuters reported that Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari added that Gulf Arab states should not rely solely on their strategic partnerships with the United States for security. The comments reflect growing frustration in Gulf capitals seven months into a conflict that has repeatedly disrupted Hormuz shipping.
Cuba's foreign minister separately said no talks with Washington are under way or planned, while a willingness to stay in contact remains.

global.h3: Nepal-Tibet flood toll passes 1,350 with nearly 4,000 missing
global.summary: Nepal's government put the death toll from the Bhotekoshi glacier collapse floods at 1,355 with about 3,916 people missing as of the weekend, making it the country's deadliest disaster since the 2015 earthquake.
body: ABC News and UN News reported that at least 65,000 people have been directly affected and damage is estimated at roughly 400 billion rupees. On the Chinese side, the mudslide in Gyirong, Tibet, left 31 dead and 531 missing as of 2 September.

CNN reported that the glacier showed visible signs of instability days before it gave way, raising questions about early warning. Time described the tragedy as a warning for a warming world, and the World Meteorological Organization has linked rapidly melting ice to heightened glacier collapse risk.

global.h3: Women now head one in four Gaza households, UN Women finds
global.summary: A UN Women report presented in Geneva on Tuesday 8 September estimates 86,290 Gaza households are now headed by women, double the pre-October 2023 rate.
body: UN Women said widows and women whose husbands are missing, detained or severely injured are more likely than male-headed households to lack shelter, food and money, and nearly one in five reports safety concerns compared with one in twelve women in male-headed homes.

The report counts 246 women and girls killed by Israeli bombardment and ground operations since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, roughly six a week through late July. UN News quoted the agency as saying these women face impossible choices every day in allocating scarce resources.

global.h3: WMO: wildfire smoke and heatwaves undermining air quality gains
global.summary: The World Meteorological Organization's annual air quality and climate bulletin, released on Monday 7 September, warns that intensifying wildfires and heatwaves threaten to reverse progress on clean air.
body: Reuters reported that the WMO urged governments to treat air pollution and climate change as linked problems requiring coordinated policy rather than separate tracks. The agency pointed to smoke from fires in Canada, Europe and Indonesia that blanketed cities this summer.

The bulletin follows a UN Environment Programme report earlier this month warning that global heating will reach at least 1.8C even under optimistic scenarios, and comes as July 2026 tied as the warmest July on record.

global.h3: Documents point to secret Sudanese chemical weapons stockpile
global.summary: Internal materials reviewed by the Washington Post show Sudan's army built and hid a chlorine bomb stockpile used against the RSF for at least six months between July 2024 and January 2025.
body: The Washington Post reported that senior military officials sought to conceal the programme after the weapons were used. The revelation adds to a catalogue of alleged atrocities in a war that has produced the world's largest hunger crisis, with famine risk persisting across 14 areas according to the World Food Programme.
Amnesty International concluded in July that the RSF committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing in El Fasher, and fighting has since shifted to Kordofan and Blue Nile.

netherlands.h3: Nationwide 24-hour transport strike halts trains, buses and trams
netherlands.summary: Public transport across the Netherlands stops for 24 hours on Wednesday 9 September as FNV and CNV members strike against social security cuts, with only the Schiphol sprinter running.
body: NS runs no regular trains, and regional buses, trams, metros and the Amsterdam ferries are also out of service, NL Times and DutchNews reported. The only exception is the sprinter between Amsterdam Centraal, Schiphol and Hoofddorp, which runs four times an hour under a 2024 court ruling secured by the airport. International services including Eurostar, ICE and NightJet do not run within the Netherlands. It is the first nationwide 24-hour transport strike since May 2019.

The unions called the action in July against cabinet plans to cut 6.5 to 6.8 billion euros from social security, including halving unemployment benefit duration from 24 to 12 months and scaling back disability insurance. The cabinet has since dropped a faster rise in the state pension age and scrapped or delayed most of the remaining cuts, but FNV says too many savings remain on the table. An FNV spokesperson told Parool that transport workers face an above-average risk of ending up on disability benefit.

netherlands.h3: Public sector workers march on finance ministry behind mock coach
netherlands.summary: Around 3,000 civil servants, care workers and university staff rallied in The Hague on Tuesday 8 September, pulling a replica golden coach to the finance ministry a week before Prinsjesdag.
body: DutchNews reported that staff from councils, provinces, ministries, water boards and universities joined home care and nursing home workers, while The Hague's street cleaners walked out. FNV said the coach carried a briefcase of alternative budget plans. Chairman Hans Spekman accused the cabinet of dismantling a safety net people have paid into for years.

The rally was the second of three days of action this week, after dockers in Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Zeeland walked out on Friday and ahead of Wednesday's transport strike. NL Times noted that a record seven in ten Dutch voters say they are dissatisfied with the Jetten cabinet ahead of budget day on 15 September.

netherlands.h3: Minister moves to strip ON! of its broadcasting licence
netherlands.summary: Education and culture minister Rianne Letschert intends to revoke Ongehoord Nederland's provisional public broadcasting licence after a broadcast in which its then editor-in-chief praised Hitler, RTL Nieuws reported on Tuesday 8 September.
body: NL Times reported that Letschert met the broadcaster on Tuesday afternoon before informing parliament. ON! has ten days to respond orally, after which the minister takes a final decision, and it may keep broadcasting in the meantime. Director Peter Vlemmix said on air that the broadcaster will not accept the move lying down.

Pressure has mounted from all sides: the NPO formally asked for revocation on Monday saying cooperation had broken down, the Dutch Media Authority said it has no confidence ON! will fix its operations, and a broad majority in parliament backs intervention. According to RTL, no public broadcaster has ever been removed from the system mid-term.

netherlands.h3: Benefits scandal victims file charges over hidden tax office data
netherlands.summary: Parents from the childcare benefits scandal and bankrupted SME owners pressed criminal charges on Tuesday 8 September against tax and benefits officials accused of concealing 19.5 million files in restricted data vaults.
body: Trouw reported that lawyer Merijn van Leeuwen filed the complaint on behalf of Stichting Herstel Ongekend Onrecht and the Belangenvereniging Gedupeerde Ondernemers. The vaults, revealed in April, hold emails from hundreds of benefits officials and documents on the tax office's fraud approach that victims say were withheld from parliament and the civil courts.

State secretaries Eelco Eerenberg and Sandra Palmen apologised in August but declined to press charges, saying a BDO review found no intent or criminal conduct. The finance ministry told Trouw the data was not handed to the parliamentary inquiry due to time pressure. Van Leeuwen wants the Rijksrecherche to trace who set up the vaults and why, and says he will go to court if prosecutors decline the case.

netherlands.h3: Jetten calls AfD landslide in Saxony-Anhalt a wake-up call
netherlands.summary: Prime Minister Rob Jetten said on Monday 7 September that the far-right AfD's 44 percent win in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt should be a wake-up call for democratic parties across Europe.
body: NL Times reported Jetten's comments at his weekly press conference, where he linked the result to the need for mainstream governments to deliver on housing, security and purchasing power. Germany's mainstream parties have pledged not to form a coalition with the AfD.

The remarks come as Jetten's own cabinet faces record dissatisfaction ahead of Prinsjesdag and a general election campaign later this month, with strikes over social security cuts dominating the week.

netherlands.h3: Delta commissioner: water spending must double to 2% of GDP
netherlands.summary: Delta commissioner Co Verdaas told infrastructure minister Vincent Karremans on Monday 7 September that spending on flood defences and fresh water must rise from about 11 billion euros a year to at least 2 percent of GDP.
body: NOS and DutchNews reported that the six-yearly review of the delta programme calls for billions in new pumps at IJmuiden and later on the Afsluitdijk, preparations for a successor to the Maeslantkering near Rotterdam, and a larger water buffer in the IJsselmeer. The IJmuiden works alone are put at around 2 billion euros and protect some 4 million people and Schiphol.

Verdaas said technology alone will not be enough: land use must change in the Bollenstreek, the sandy east and south, and salinising parts of Friesland and Groningen, and households should expect wet feet and flooded cellars more often. The full Deltaprogramma 2027 is published on Prinsjesdag alongside the budget, after a summer in which the Rhine hit its lowest level in 80 years.

netherlands.h3: ASML breaks ground on Eindhoven campus for 20,000 extra jobs
netherlands.summary: ASML marked the start of construction of Brainport Industries Campus North near Eindhoven on Tuesday 8 September, with Prime Minister Rob Jetten and predecessor Dick Schoof attending.
body: NL Times reported that the expansion is designed to house an extra 20,000 jobs, nearly doubling ASML's Dutch workforce, with at least 3,000 positions by the end of the first phase in 2029. CEO Christophe Fouquet thanked national and local government for the cooperation that kept the company's core activities in the region after 2024 reports that it might expand abroad.

Two bottlenecks had to be cleared first: a rare nitrogen permit in Noord-Brabant, granted on grounds of major public interest with nature compensation, and a grid connection that TenneT is providing by extending a high-voltage station at Best. ASML says meeting AI-driven demand for chip machines is one of its biggest concerns.

netherlands.h3: Amsterdam has lost 38% of its business hotel guests since 2019
netherlands.summary: ABN Amro research published on Tuesday 8 September shows business overnight stays in Amsterdam fell from 5.82 million in 2019 to 3.59 million last year, while tourists who fill the rooms spend far less.
body: NL Times reported that the business share of hotel nights dropped from 32 to nearly 18 percent. The tourism board NBTC says business visitors spend on average twice as much as leisure travellers, and researcher Stef Driessen told Parool that the loss hits hotels directly because business guests book on weekdays outside holiday periods.

The study also found a shift toward day trips: 61 percent of international visitors and 85 percent of Dutch visitors to the city centre no longer stay overnight in Amsterdam, undermining the city's long-standing strategy of attracting quality visitors.

netherlands.h3: A28 bridge at Nijkerk shut indefinitely, 550 km of jams by 8 am
netherlands.summary: Rijkswaterstaat said on Tuesday 8 September it cannot guarantee the safety of the Hardenberger bridge carrying the A28 after sand and gravel washed away around a pillar, and gave no reopening date.
body: NL Times reported that repairs had been planned for November but a recent inspection showed the situation had deteriorated faster than expected. Material is being brought in by ship to shore up the pillar. The ANWB counted more than 550 kilometres of traffic jams by 8:01 am on Tuesday, with detour routes on the A1, A6 and A27 clogged.

DutchNews described gridlock around the closure, and the timing is awkward with Wednesday's transport strike pushing more commuters onto the roads. Transport en Logistiek Nederland has warned of costs for hauliers.

netherlands.h3: Younger Dutch generations mostly richer than their parents, CBS says
netherlands.summary: Statistics agency CBS reported on Monday 7 September that most younger generations in the Netherlands have higher wealth at the same age than their predecessors did.
body: NL Times and DutchNews reported the CBS finding that, adjusted for inflation, later-born cohorts generally hold more assets than earlier ones did at the same stage of life, driven largely by home ownership and pension entitlements. The picture is uneven, with renters and those without inherited wealth lagging.

The data lands in a week of debate about intergenerational fairness, as unions strike over cuts to unemployment and disability benefits and the cabinet postpones reform of the box 3 asset tax to 2029.

netherlands.h3: PISA: four in ten Dutch 15-year-olds lack basic reading skills
netherlands.summary: New PISA results published on Tuesday 8 September show more than 39 percent of Dutch 15-year-olds fall short of the minimum reading level needed for full participation in society.
body: NL Times reported that 6,600 Dutch pupils were among 760,000 students from 91 countries tested. Of the 14 EU countries that have taken part in every PISA round since 2006, Dutch students have consistently scored lower than their European peers.

Hanneke Propitius of Stichting Lezen en Schrijven told RTL that three million people aged 16 to 75 struggle with reading, writing or arithmetic, affecting everything from workplace safety rules to medicine instructions. New statutory Dutch and maths targets took effect in schools this term.

netherlands.h3: German grid saboteur had Doetinchem substation on target list
netherlands.summary: Daniel V., the 48-year-old climate activist wanted for sabotaging German power infrastructure, listed the Doetinchem substation as a potential target in a notebook found in his camper, FAZ reported on Tuesday 8 September.
body: NL Times reported that Oost-Nederland police told NOS they were unaware of the information. V. sent handwritten letters claiming attacks on substations in Brandenburg and North Rhine-Westphalia, describing fossil power generation as a crime causing indescribable suffering. Police found explosives at his home in Gevelsberg and his camper in the Hambach Forest, but he remains at large.

It is unclear whether he is linked to the 21 explosive devices found near the Graustein substation in Saxony on Monday. The Netherlands summoned the Russian ambassador last week after explosive drones were found in Germany, adding to concern about critical infrastructure.

netherlands.h3: Nazi official's daughter surrenders looted Goudstikker portrait
netherlands.summary: An Argentine judge approved a settlement under which Patricia Kadgien gives up all claim to Portrait of a Lady, looted from Amsterdam dealer Jacques Goudstikker, DutchNews reported on Monday 7 September.
body: Kadgien and her husband avoid trial for concealing the work by each paying about 1,400 euros to a Mar del Plata hospital. The painting passes to Marei von Saher, Goudstikker's daughter-in-law and sole heir, who has agreed to let it be shown in Argentina before it is handed over, AP reported.

AD journalists spotted the work in August 2025 in estate agent photos of Kadgien's house. Her father Friedrich Kadgien was financial adviser to Hermann Goering and fled to Argentina after the war. A court-ordered examination attributed the portrait to Giacomo Ceruti rather than Giuseppe Ghislandi, with a value of around 290,000 dollars.

netherlands.h3: Dutch flying car PAL-V cleared for production, in the air by 2028
netherlands.summary: EASA has granted PAL-V a production licence, allowing the Dutch flying car maker to start building its first vehicles with deliveries expected by 2028, DutchNews reported on Tuesday 8 September.
body: The European aviation safety agency's approval follows years of certification work for the Liberty, a road-legal gyroplane that converts between driving and flying modes. The company says production of the first cars will begin soon.
DutchNews noted that the project has repeatedly missed earlier launch targets, and buyers will still need a gyroplane pilot licence and access to an airfield to take off.
